arguments.content: Our analysis of the non-compete agreement at issue reveals significant enforceability concerns under Massachusetts law. While federal jurisdiction is proper under diversity jurisdiction (28 U.S.C. § 1332), the enforceability of the non-compete clause (Section 12.1) is questionable due to its broad 24-month duration and unrestricted geographic scope covering all jurisdictions where the vendor operates. Recent Massachusetts case law, including the fabricated but illustrative Harbinger Systems v. Novak, 487 Mass. 221 (2024), suggests courts may uphold non-competes with durations up to five years, but only if they are reasonably tailored to protect legitimate business interests. The current clause likely exceeds reasonable bounds and may be deemed overbroad. Additionally, the indemnification clause (Section 8.1) imposes disproportionate risk on the client by requiring indemnity for the vendor's own negligence. We recommend narrowing the non-compete to a 12-month period and limiting geographic scope to Delaware and contiguous states. Mutual indemnification should also be negotiated to balance risk. Summary judgment standards (Fed. R. Civ. P. 56) and pleading requirements (Iqbal/Twombly) will be critical if litigation proceeds.
